learn.title: Second Life EV Batteries for Grid Storage
learn.intro: EV batteries after automotive use can power grids, reducing waste and costs. With 1.5 million EVs sold in India (2023), repurposing batteries extends their 8-15 year lifespan, addressing energy storage needs while cutting emissions.
learn.c1_text: After EVs retire, batteries retain 70-80% capacity. They're tested and reconfigured for stationary storage. Like a marathon runner becoming a coach, these batteries shift roles to serve communities longer.
learn.c2_text: Reusing batteries cuts costs by 30-50% vs new systems. IRENA notes 90% recycling potential. This reduces lithium mining and meets India's 500 GW renewable target (2030) with affordable storage.
learn.c3_text: India's FAME II scheme promotes second-life batteries. Tata Power and Fortis Health use retired EV batteries for hospitals. The 2023 Battery Swapping Policy supports this model, aligning with India's 500 TWh renewable energy target by 2030.
learn.stat2: Second-life batteries cost 30-50% less than new
learn.stat3: 90% of battery materials can be recycled
learn.stat4: India's renewable energy target: 500 GW by 2030

learn.title: Agrivoltaics: Solar and Farming Together
learn.intro: Agrivoltaics combines solar panels with agriculture, boosting land productivity. With India's solar potential at 750 GW, this dual-use approach addresses food-water-energy security while maximizing limited arable land.
learn.c1_text: Solar panels are elevated to allow crop growth beneath. Crops like tomatoes and lettuce thrive under partial shade, increasing yields by 20-60%. Like a parasol protecting a picnic, panels shield crops from harsh sun.
learn.c2_text: Reduced evaporation conserves water. Panels protect crops from extreme weather. Studies show 30-60% water savings. NREL reports higher energy output in hot climates due to panel cooling effects from plant transpiration.
learn.c3_text: Telangana's 1 MW pilot farm uses bifacial panels with pomegranate cultivation. Gujarat's Kutch project combines solar with salt farming. The Ministry of New & Renewable Energy supports 50 agrivoltaic pilot projects under its Sustainable Energy Awareness Programme.

learn.title: Geothermal Energy: Earth's Heat Power
learn.intro: Geothermal energy harnesses Earth's internal heat for clean power and heating. With 90% of global geothermal potential untapped, India's 8.7 GW capacity (2023) offers baseload renewable energy, operating 24/7 unlike solar/wind.
learn.c1_text: Hot water from underground reservoirs spins turbines. Enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) drill into dry rock, creating artificial reservoirs. Like a jacuzzi's heater, Earth's magma provides constant energy without weather dependence.
learn.c2_text: Geothermal heat pumps use stable 10-15°C ground temps for efficient building heating/cooling. US DOE estimates 30-60% energy savings. District heating systems in cities like Reykjavik serve 90% of homes, reducing fossil fuel use.
learn.c3_text: India's Himalayan region holds 13,000 MW potential. Projects in Jammu's Patnitpur and Karnataka's Hosahalli aim for 1 GW by 2030. The Ministry's Geothermal Policy 2023 targets 10 GW capacity, supporting rural electrification and green cooking solutions.

learn.title: Direct Air Carbon Capture Technology
learn.intro: Direct Air Capture (DAC) removes CO2 directly from the atmosphere using renewable energy. With global DAC capacity at 0.15 Mt/year, this technology is critical for India's net-zero 2070 goal, offsetting hard-to-abate sectors like aviation and cement.
learn.c1_text: Fans pull air through filters or chemicals that bind CO2. Renewable energy powers the process. Climeworks' Orca plant captures 4,000 tons/year. Like a vacuum cleaner for emissions, DAC treats entire atmosphere rather than point sources.
learn.c2_text: DAC requires 300-600 kWh per ton of CO2. IEA estimates costs at $600-1,000/ton today, falling to $150-300 by 2030 with scaling. India's renewable energy costs make DAC viable for carbon-neutral industries by 2040.
learn.c3_text: India's Nationally Determined Contribution includes DAC pilots under its Green Growth Initiative. IIT Madras partners with Global Thermostat for a 10,000-ton/year plant by 2026. The 2023 Hydrogen Mission allocates funding for DAC-integrated hydrogen production.
learn.stat2: DAC requires 300-600 kWh per ton CO2

learn.title: Climate Finance and COP Agreements
learn.intro: Climate finance channels funds to developing nations for clean energy transitions. With $100 billion/year pledged, COP27's Loss and Damage Fund addresses climate impacts. India's $2.5 billion climate commitment supports 500 GW renewables, bridging global equity gaps.
learn.c1_text: The GCF provides grants/low-interest loans for mitigation/adaptation. India received $500 million for solar parks. Like a bank for the planet, it prioritizes vulnerable nations, with 50% funding for adaptation projects in Africa and Asia.
learn.c2_text: COP27 established a fund for irreversible climate damage. IEA estimates $300 billion/year needed by 2030. India's 2023 proposal for a $10 billion South Asian hub addresses monsoon failures and cyclones, supporting resilient infrastructure.
learn.c3_text: India's $2.5 billion climate finance pledge under COP26 funds 500 GW renewables. The National Climate Fund supports 100 villages with solar microgrids. India leads in solar manufacturing, exporting technology to 30 countries through the International Solar Alliance.
learn.stat3: Loss and Damage Fund target: $10 billion hub

learn.title: Types of Solar Panels Compared
learn.intro: Solar panels come in three main types: monocrystalline, polycrystalline, and thin-film. With India's 60 GW solar installed (2024), understanding efficiency and cost differences helps choose the right system for households, industries, or utilities.
learn.c1_text: Monocrystalline (20-22% efficiency) uses single silicon crystals, appearing black. Polycrystalline (15-17% efficiency) is cheaper blue-tinted. Like wine vs beer, mono is premium but pricier; poly offers value for large installations.
learn.c2_text: Thin-film (10-12% efficiency) uses layers on glass, flexible and lightweight. First Solar's panels last 30+ years. Like a sticker on a window, thin-film adapts to curved surfaces, ideal for buildings and deserts with high temperatures.
learn.c3_text: India's 60 GW solar target (2024) prioritizes domestic manufacturing under Make in India. Tata Power Solar leads with monocrystalline tech. State subsidies cover 30-40% costs for residential rooftop systems, boosting adoption in rural areas.
